q: The IUPAC name of the alkane is
question: The IUPAC name of the alkane is
solution:
The longest continuous carbon chain contains $8$ carbon atoms, so the parent hydrocarbon is octane.

There are five methyl groups attached to this chain. Numbering from the left gives the locants $2,3,3,7,7$, whereas numbering from the right gives $2,2,6,6,7$.

We choose $2,2,6,6,7$ because, at the first point of difference, $2$ is smaller than $3$.

Hence, the IUPAC name is $2,2,6,6,7$-pentamethyloctane — Option D.

q: Which of the following compound has all four type (1°, 2°, 3°, 4°) of carbon atoms?
question: Which of the following compound has all four type (1°, 2°, 3°, 4°) of carbon atoms?
solution:
• Primary ($1^\circ$) carbon is attached to only one other carbon atom.

  • Secondary ($2^\circ$) carbon is attached to two other carbon atoms.

  • Tertiary ($3^\circ$) carbon is attached to three other carbon atoms.

  • Quaternary ($4^\circ$) carbon is attached to four other carbon atoms.

Now, look at the given options:

Option A: 2,3,4-trimethylpentane

The carbon atoms in this molecule are either attached to one other carbon (the terminal and branch methyl groups, making them $1^\circ$) or attached to three other carbons ($3^\circ$). It does not contain any $2^\circ$ or $4^\circ$ carbon atoms.

Option B: 2,2,3-trimethylpentane

Since this molecule contains $1^\circ$, $2^\circ$, $3^\circ$, and $4^\circ$ carbon atoms, it has all four types.

question: The correct IUPAC name of given structure is
solution:
The longest continuous carbon chain contains $10$ carbon atoms, so the parent hydrocarbon is decane.

There are two substituents on this chain:

  • An ethyl group, $-\mathrm{CH_2CH_3}$.

  • A branched group, $-\mathrm{CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3}$. Numbering this group from its point of attachment gives a propyl chain with methyl groups at positions $1$ and $2$. It is called 1,2-dimethylpropyl.

Numbering the parent chain from either end gives the locants $5$ and $6$. The tie is resolved by giving the lower locant to the substituent cited first alphabetically. Here, dimethylpropyl comes before ethyl; “di” is included when alphabetising a complex substituent.

Thus, the correct name is 5-(1,2-dimethylpropyl)-6-ethyldecane — Option C.

Column-I Column-II
(P) Neopentane (1) 2,2,4-trimethylpentane
(Q) Isohexane (2) 2,2-dimethylpropane
(R) Neohexane (3) 2-methylpentane
(S) Isooctane (4) 2,2-dimethylbutane

Choose the correct option from the options given below.
solution:
(P) Neopentane

The prefix neo- indicates a quaternary carbon (a central carbon bonded to four other methyl groups). Neopentane has a total of five carbon atoms:

The longest continuous carbon chain has three carbon atoms (propane), with two methyl groups at carbon-2.

Thus, its IUPAC name is 2,2-dimethylpropane.

So, P → 2.

(Q) Isohexane

The prefix iso- means there is a methyl branch at the second carbon of the chain. Isohexane contains a total of six carbon atoms:

The longest chain contains five carbon atoms (pentane), with a single methyl group at position 2.

Thus, its IUPAC name is 2-methylpentane.

So, Q → 3.

(R) Neohexane

Neohexane has six carbon atoms in total, featuring a quaternary carbon near one end:

The longest chain contains four carbon atoms (butane), with two methyl groups at carbon-2.

Thus, its IUPAC name is 2,2-dimethylbutane.

So, R → 4.

(S) Isooctane

Isooctane is the common name used historically for the branched octane isomer used as an octane rating standard:

The longest chain contains five carbon atoms (pentane). Numbering from the left gives substituents at positions 2, 2, and 4.

Thus, its IUPAC name is 2,2,4-trimethylpentane.

So, S → 1.

Combining all matches:

P → 2, Q → 3, R → 4, S → 1

The correct option is Option B.

q: The sum of numerical values of given compound's IUPAC name is
question: The sum of numerical values of given compound's IUPAC name is
solution:
Compound (A)

  • The principal ring is a six-membered carbon ring: cyclohexane.

  • There are two methyl substituents attached to the same ring carbon.

  • Following the lowest locant rule, this carbon is assigned position $1$.

IUPAC Name: 1,1-dimethylcyclohexane

Numerical values: $1, 1$

$$\text{Sum for (A)} = 1 + 1 = 2$$

Compound (B)

  • The principal ring is cyclohexane.

  • Substituents present on the ring:

  • Two methyl groups at one carbon.

  • One ethyl group at an adjacent carbon.

  • Two methyl groups at the carbon opposite to the first.

  • To achieve the lowest set of locants:

  • Assign position $1$ to the ring carbon carrying two methyl groups adjacent to the ethyl group.

  • Numbering clockwise gives position $2$ to the ethyl group and position $4$ to the carbon carrying the other two methyl groups.

  • This yields the locant set $(1, 1, 2, 4, 4)$, which is lower than any alternate numbering such as $(1, 1, 3, 4, 4)$.

  • Arranging substituents alphabetically, "ethyl" precedes "methyl".

IUPAC Name: 2-ethyl-1,1,4,4-tetramethylcyclohexane

Numerical values: $2, 1, 1, 4, 4$

$$\text{Sum for (B)} = 2 + 1 + 1 + 4 + 4 = 12$$

Compound (C)

  • The structure is:

    $$\mathrm{(CH_3CH_2)_2CH-CH(CH_3)_2}$$

  • The longest continuous carbon chain contains $5$ carbon atoms: pentane.

  • Numbering from the right-hand side gives substituents at positions $2$ and $3$, giving the lowest locant set $(2, 3)$ rather than $(3, 4)$:

  • Position $2$ has a methyl substituent.

  • Position $3$ has an ethyl substituent.

  • Writing the substituents in alphabetical order gives "ethyl" before "methyl".

IUPAC Name: 3-ethyl-2-methylpentane

Numerical values: $3, 2$

$$\text{Sum for (C)} = 3 + 2 = 5$$

Total Sum

Adding the numerical values from all three compounds:

$$\text{Total Sum} = 2 + 12 + 5 = 19$$
